questions.question: What is the key difference between adoption from foster care and infant adoption?
questions.correctAnswer: Foster care adoption gives a permanent home to a child already in the state foster care system whose birth parents' rights have been ended by a court, while infant adoption is usually a voluntary placement of a newborn arranged before or shortly after birth
distractors: Foster care adoption is always temporary, while infant adoption is the only kind that a court can make permanent
Infant adoption involves children who are waiting in state custody, while foster care adoption involves only newborns
There is no real difference - the two terms describe exactly the same process with the same steps and timelines
questions.explanation: Children in foster care are in state custody, often because of abuse or neglect, and adoption becomes an option only after a court has terminated the birth parents' rights and reunification is no longer possible; many waiting children are older, part of a sibling group, or have special needs. Infant adoption, by contrast, usually begins with a birth parent voluntarily making an adoption plan during pregnancy or soon after delivery, with placement arranged through an agency or an attorney.
questions.memoryHook: Foster adoption starts with a child already waiting in state care - infant adoption starts with a voluntary plan for a newborn!

questions.question: What do kinship adoption and stepparent adoption have in common?
questions.correctAnswer: In both, the child is adopted by someone who already has a family connection to the child - a relative such as a grandparent or aunt in kinship adoption, or the spouse of a parent in stepparent adoption
distractors: In both, the adoptive parents must live in a different country from the child until the adoption is final
In both, the child must first spend at least two years in a stranger foster home before any relative may adopt
In both, no court is ever involved, because family members can transfer parental rights with a handshake agreement
questions.explanation: Kinship (relative) adoption and stepparent adoption are called intrafamily adoptions because the adopters are already part of the child's family. Keeping a child with relatives can preserve family bonds, culture, and a sense of identity when birth parents cannot provide care. These adoptions still go through a court, and requirements such as a home study and background checks still apply, although some steps may be simplified compared with an unrelated adoption.
questions.memoryHook: Kinship and stepparent adoption keep a child inside the family they already know!

questions.question: What extra legal layer does international adoption add compared with a domestic adoption?
questions.correctAnswer: The family must satisfy the laws of both the child's country of origin and the United States, including U.S. immigration rules that allow the child to enter and live in the country
distractors: No extra layer - a family can bring a child home from another country with only a passport and a plane ticket
The child must give up any chance of U.S. citizenship permanently as a condition of the adoption
Only the other country's laws apply, so U.S. courts and agencies play no role at any point
questions.explanation: In an international (intercountry) adoption, two legal systems are involved: the child's birth country decides whether the child may be adopted and leave, and the United States requires its own approvals, including a home study, federal review of the family's eligibility, and an immigrant visa for the child. International treaties such as the Hague Adoption Convention add safeguards meant to prevent child trafficking and to make sure adoptions are ethical and in the child's best interest.
questions.memoryHook: International adoption means two countries' rules - plus U.S. immigration approval!

questions.question: What is a home study in the adoption process?
questions.correctAnswer: A structured assessment of the prospective parents and their home - interviews, home visits, background and child-abuse registry checks, health and financial review, references, and required training - used to judge readiness to adopt
distractors: A homework assignment the adopted child completes during the first school term in the new home
A simple house-cleaning inspection that checks only whether the home is tidy on the day of the visit
An optional meet-and-greet dinner that families may skip if an agency worker already knows them socially
questions.explanation: The home study is completed before a child is placed and must be finished before an adoption can move forward. In Louisiana, the study includes consultation visits and interviews with everyone living in the home, state and national criminal background checks, and a review of the family's motivation, health, income, and living environment; for foster and adoptive certification through the state, required training is part of the process. The written study is reviewed by the agency and the court as evidence that the placement will be safe and stable.
questions.memoryHook: A home study checks the people and the home - interviews, visits, background checks, and training!

questions.question: How does an adoption become legally complete?
questions.correctAnswer: After placement and a supervised period in the home, a judge reviews the case and issues a final adoption decree in court; from that point the child is legally the child of the adoptive parents, with the same rights as a child born to them
distractors: Automatically on the day the child first spends a night in the adoptive home, with no court involvement at any stage
When the agency sends the family a congratulatory letter, which carries the same legal force as a court order
Only when the adopted child turns 18 and signs paperwork confirming the adoption as an adult
questions.explanation: Finalization is the court step that ends the adoption process. Before it, the child lives in the home for a supervised period (for a Louisiana foster care adoption, at least six months) while a caseworker visits and reports on how the placement is going; an adoption petition is then filed, and a judge grants the final decree if the adoption serves the child's best interest. After finalization, a new birth certificate can be issued naming the adoptive parents, and the legal parent-child relationship is permanent.
questions.memoryHook: An adoption is complete when a judge signs the final decree - permanent in law, not just in the home!

questions.question: Which resources help people learn about, pursue, or get support for adoption?
questions.correctAnswer: Public help through the state child welfare agency (in Louisiana, the Department of Children and Family Services, which handles foster care adoption), licensed private adoption agencies, adoption attorneys, and support services such as post-adoption support groups and adoption subsidies for children adopted from foster care
distractors: Only private agencies that charge large fees - public agencies are legally barred from any role in adoption
Social media groups alone, because licensed agencies and state offices are not permitted to give adoption information
Hospitals only - once a family leaves the hospital, no organization anywhere provides adoption information or support
questions.explanation: Adoption resources come in public and private forms. Louisiana's Department of Children and Family Services (DCFS) recruits and certifies foster and adoptive families, matches waiting children, and administers adoption assistance (subsidies) that help families meet the needs of children adopted from foster care, which typically costs little or nothing compared with private infant adoption. Licensed private agencies and adoption attorneys handle many infant and international placements, and counselors, support groups, and pregnancy resource services provide information and support to expectant parents considering an adoption plan - a resources topic Louisiana's adoption awareness law (RS 17:263) names for classroom instruction.
questions.memoryHook: Start public with DCFS for foster adoption, or licensed private agencies and attorneys for other paths - support exists on every route!

questions.question: What benefits of adoption are documented for children, families, and society?
questions.correctAnswer: Children gain a permanent, legally secure family and stability when their birth parents cannot care for them; adoptive families gain the chance to parent; and society benefits when children waiting in foster care move into permanent homes instead of growing up in temporary care
distractors: The only documented benefit is financial - adoptive parents are guaranteed a profit from adopting a child
Adoption has no measurable effect on a child's stability, because legal permanence does not change a child's living situation
Children in foster care are better off staying in temporary placements indefinitely, so permanency is not considered a benefit
questions.explanation: Permanency is the central benefit researchers and child welfare agencies point to: a child who is adopted has legal security, a stable home, and lifelong family membership, instead of repeated moves between temporary foster placements. Adoption also lets people who cannot have children biologically - or who choose to parent a waiting child - build a family, and it reduces the number of children who age out of foster care without a permanent family, an outcome linked to higher risks of homelessness and unemployment. Louisiana's adoption awareness law (RS 17:263) lists the benefits of adoption among the topics students should learn.
questions.memoryHook: Adoption's core benefit is permanency - a stable, legal, lifelong family for a child who needs one!

questions.question: Under Louisiana's Safe Haven Law, what may a parent who cannot care for a newborn do?
questions.correctAnswer: Safely hand the infant (up to 60 days old) to an employee at a designated Safe Haven site - such as a hospital, a staffed fire station, or a staffed law enforcement station - or call 911, remaining anonymous and without fear of prosecution, so the baby gets immediate care and can be placed for adoption
distractors: Leave the baby unattended on any doorstep or in any public place, which the law treats exactly the same as a Safe Haven handover
Wait until the baby is six months old, because Safe Haven sites are forbidden to accept any infant younger than that
Give the baby to any stranger who offers to take the child, since the law protects every informal handover equally
questions.explanation: Louisiana's Safe Haven Law (Children's Code Articles 1149-1160) exists to prevent unsafe abandonment. A parent may leave an unharmed infant no more than 60 days old with an employee of a designated emergency care facility - a licensed hospital, certain clinics during operating hours, a manned fire station, or a manned law enforcement station - or in an authorized newborn safety device, and a parent who cannot travel may call 911 so responders come to them. Relinquishment done this way is not a crime and can be anonymous; the infant receives medical care, the Department of Children and Family Services takes custody, and the child can move toward a permanent adoptive home.
questions.memoryHook: Safe Haven means hand the baby to a person at a safe site - up to 60 days, anonymous, no prosecution!
